results.title: Mid-Season Highs & Lows
results.description: We are halfway through the season, and our Bills are 7-1 for the first time since 1993. Sounds like a reason to celebrate. I thought at best the Bills would be 6-2 at this point, at worst 5-3. Joe Brady has answered the call and Josh Allen and the offense are humming right along, it hasn't always been pretty, but when the game is on the line and the Bills need to score, I feel confident that the Bills can score at any moment. The defense, as expected, is a work-in-progress. Giving up lots of points early was concerning. Have these last two games shown that the defense is turning things around? We shall see. Especially now that we've added Amani Hooker. I wanted to get your thoughts on the highs and lows of the team. Highs: Tyler Bass. His kicks can still be entertaining, but give this guy credit, he has rebounded in a big way. Bravo, Bass-O-Matic! Keon Coleman: He is not a #1 WR, but his play has been tremendous. Little to complain about. Greg Rousseau: This is an easy choice, but seeing Groot play the way he has consistently, has been amazing. DJ Moore: When he's on the field, he is a difference maker. Josh Allen: Another obvious choice, but he is the team, a star. He does make some odd decisions, but when the game is on the line, we can count on him. Ty Johnson: He still is a great option as a running back & receiver. James Cook: The fumbles have been rough however he is our top runner and he's always giving his all. Watching how shifty he is and how he can break through the line is fantastic. Deone Walker & Ed Oliver: They may not get a ton of stats, but they are monsters. Christian Benford: Struggled early, but has come back strong after his injury, and is showing why he's our top Cornerback. Davison Igbinosun: By far our top rookie. Had some penalty issues, but he looks very comfortable in coverage, and has been a good defender. Joe Brady: Some cute and questionable playcalling still happens, but he does play to the strengths of the offense. I also appreciate how he treated James Cook during his fumbling issues. Instead of having him sit on the sidelines for a quarter, he showed how much he trusted him by sending him back out there. Starting Offensive Line: Not much to complain about with this group. Halftime Adjustments: Whatever they are feeding the team at halftime, keep giving it to them. Lows: Penalties: Crazy amount early this season. This has to be fixed. CJ Gardner-Johnson: I really thought he would be the leader in our secondary. Joshua Palmer: I thought we would see a rebound from this guy. Michael Hoecht: I guess this is what happens to a player after an achilles injury. Aside from being a Special Teams demon, he's done little. Javon Solomon: Yes, he's not a starter, but this is his third season with the team, and all I see is a Special Teamer. Jackson Hawes: Penalties have been a killer for him. Definitely has taken a step back. That's how I see it. What's your takeaway?
